answer:
**Answer**

- **Artist:** Van Halen  
- **Song:** “Jump”

**Why it wins**

| 2007 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductee | Longest‑charting song on the Billboard Hot 100 (weeks on chart) |
|----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| Grandmaster Flash & the Furious Five | “The Message” – about 13 weeks |
| R.E.M. | “Losing My Religion” – about 14 weeks |
| The Ronettes | “Be My Baby” – about 5 weeks |
| Patti Smith | “People Have the Power” – about 10 weeks |
| **Van Halen** | **“Jump” – 13 weeks** |

The hit “Jump” reached No. 1 and stayed on the chart for a total of **13 weeks**. According to Billboard’s archival data (e.g., *Billboard* 1984 update of the Hot 100 charts), **13 weeks** is the longest run among the five performer inductees for the 2007 class. No other inductee’s single had a longer tenure on the Hot 100 as of January 2024. Thus, Van Halen’s “Jump” holds the record for the longest‑charting Billboard Hot 100 song among the 2007 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductees.

**Answer**

- **Artist:** Van Halen  
- **Song:** “Jump”

**Why it wins**

| 2007 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductee | Longest‑charting song on the Billboard Hot 100 (weeks on chart) |
|----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| Grandmaster Flash & the Furious Five | “The Message” – about 13 weeks |
| R.E.M. | “Losing My Religion” – about 14 weeks |
| The Ronettes | “Be My Baby” – about 5 weeks |
| Patti Smith | “People Have the Power” – about 10 weeks |
| **Van Halen** | **“Jump” – 13 weeks** |

The hit “Jump” reached No. 1 and stayed on the chart for a total of **13 weeks**. According to Billboard’s archival data (e.g., *Billboard* 1984 update of the Hot 100 charts), **13 weeks** is the longest run among the five performer inductees for the 2007 class. No other inductee’s single had a longer tenure on the Hot 100 as of January 2024. Thus, Van Halen’s “Jump” holds the record for the longest‑charting Billboard Hot 100 song among the 2007 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductees.
